One word substitutions.question:
১) Choose the correct alternative which can be substituted for the below underlined phrase. (1-3)
Several tribes, who were the earliest inhabitants of Australia, are extant till today.
One word substitutions.exp:
aboriginal: আদিবাসী
endemic: স্থানীয়
contiguous : সংলগ্ন

One word substitutions.question: ২) At the haunted house a series of events took place, which <u>could not be explained</u>
One word substitutions.exp: Which <u>could not be explained</u>, that was inexplicable.

One word substitutions.question: ৩) The parents attending the meeting were <u>hostile and aggressive</u>. This set the mood of the unfortunate meeting.
One word substitutions.exp:
Belligerent - যুদ্ধমান
Shrewd - বিচক্ষণ
Docile - শিক্ষাগ্রহণে তত্পর, অনুগত
Timorous - ভীরু, সশঙ্ক

One word substitutions.question: ৪) Large scale departure of people-
One word substitutions.exp:
Migration: seasonal movement of animals from one region to another.
Emigration: the act of leaving one's own country to settle permanently in another; moving abroad.
Immigration: the action of coming to live permanently in a foreign country.
Exodus: a mass departure of people.

One word substitutions.question: ৫) A person who has no money to pay off his debts-
One word substitutions.exp:
Debtor: a person, country, or organization that owes money.
Pauper: a very poor person.
Beggar: a person, typically a homeless one, who lives by asking for money or food.
Insolvent: unable to pay debts owed.

One word substitutions.question: ৬) Interval between two events or two periods of time of different character-
One word substitutions.exp:
Intermission: a pause or break.
Interlude: an intervening period of time; an interval.
Interpolation: the insertion of something of a different nature into something else.
Appendix: a section or table of subsidiary matter at the end of a book or document

One word substitutions.question: ৭) To come as a settler into another country-
One word substitutions.exp:
Alienate: make (someone) feel isolated or estranged.
Emigrate: leave one's own country in order to settle permanently in another.
Migrate: (of an animal, typically a bird or fish) move from one region or habitat to another according to the seasons.
Immigrate: come to live permanently in a foreign country.

One word substitutions.question: ৮) The power of reading the thoughts of others-
One word substitutions.exp:
Psychopathy: mental illness or disorder.
Telecommunication: communication over a distance by cable, telegraph, telephone, or broadcasting.
Psychology: the scientific study of the human mind and its functions, especially those affecting behaviour in a given context.
Telepathy: the supposed communication of thoughts or ideas by means other than the known senses.

One word substitutions.question: ৯) A speech delivered without any prior preparation-
One word substitutions.exp: Extempore : উপস্থিতমত, পূর্বাহ্নে প্রস্তুতহীন

One word substitutions.question: ১০) A word meaning happy and joyful-
One word substitutions.exp: While infuriated means angry, despondent means sad. Exhilarated is the right choice.

One word substitutions.question: ১১) Fear of spiders is known as-
One word substitutions.exp:
Phobia is derived from Phobos which is a Greek word for fear.
While social phobia is fear of social interaction.
Agoraphobia is fear of crowded places. Arachnophobia is fear of spiders while Hydro means water so Hydrophobia is fear of water.

One word substitutions.question: ১২) 'General pardon of political offenders' is also called as ________.
One word substitutions.exp:
Amnesty : General pardon of political offenders.
Despotism : It is a form of government in which a single entity rules with absolute power.
Autocracy : A government which is run by a dictator.
Magnanimity : Having generous and kind nature.

One word substitutions.question: ১৩) Place for ammunition and weapons is called as-
One word substitutions.exp:
Place for ammunition and weapons is called as Arsenal.
The meanings of other words are:
Asylum – Hospital for mad people
Archives – Place of collecting public/government/historical records.
Acoustics – Science of sound

One word substitutions.question: ১৪) Something that relates to everyone in the world-
One word substitutions.exp:
General: affecting or concerning all or most people or thing.
Common: occurring, found, or done often.
Usual: habitually or typically occurring or done.
Universal: relating to or done by all people or things in the world or in a particular group; applicable to all cases.

One word substitutions.question: ১৫) One who does not marry, especially as a religious obligation-
One word substitutions.exp:
Bachelor: a man who is not and has never been married.
Celibate: a person who abstains from marriage and sexual relations.
Virgin: a person who has never had sexual intercourse.
Recluse: a person who lives a solitary life and tends to avoid other people.

One word substitutions.question: ১৬) Ready to believe-
One word substitutions.exp:
Credulous: having or showing too great a readiness to believe things.
Credible: able to be believed
Creditable: (of a performance, effort, or action) deserving public acknowledgement and praise but not necessarily outstanding or successful.
Incredible: impossible to believe.

One word substitutions.question: ১৭) An expression of mild disapproval-
One word substitutions.exp:
Warning: advance notice of something.
Denigration: the action of unfairly criticizing someone or something.
Impertinence: lack of respect.
Reproof: an expression of blame or disapproval.

One word substitutions.question: ১৮) One who does not care for literature or art-
One word substitutions.exp:
Primitive: relating to, denoting, or preserving the character of an early stage in the evolutionary or historical development of something.
Illiterate: unable to read or write.
Philistine: hostile or indifferent to culture and the arts.
Barbarian: an uncultured or brutish person.

One word substitutions.question: ১৯) A person interested in reading books and nothing else-
One word substitutions.exp:
Bookkeeper: a person whose job is to keep records of the financial affairs of a business.
Scholar: a specialist in a particular branch of study, especially the humanities.
Bookworm: a person who enjoys reading.
Student: a person who is studying at a university or other place of higher education.

One word substitutions.question: ২০) The act of violating the sanctity of the church is-
One word substitutions.exp:
Sacrilege: The violation or profanation of anything sacred or held sacred.
Blasphemy: Impious utterance or action concerning god or sacred things.

One word substitutions.question: ২১) Giving undue favours to one's own kith and kin-
One word substitutions.exp:
Nepotism: The practice among those with power or influence of favouring relatives or friends, especially by giving them jobs.
Favouritism: The practice of giving unfair preferential treatment to one person or group at the expense of another.
Worldliness: The quality of being experienced and sophisticated.
Corruption: Dishonest or fraudulent conduct by those in power, typically involving bribery.

One word substitutions.question: ২২) To accustom oneself to a foreign climate-
One word substitutions.exp:
Adapt: make (something) suitable for a new use or purpose.
Adopt: choose to take up, follow, or use.
Accustom: make someone or something accept (something) as normal or usual.
Acclimatise: become accustomed to a new climate or new conditions.

One word substitutions.question: ২৩) A disease of mind causing an uncontrollable desire to steal-
One word substitutions.exp:
Schizophrenia: a long-term mental disorder of a type involving a breakdown in the relation between thought, emotion, and behaviour, leading to faulty perception, inappropriate actions and feelings, withdrawal from reality and personal relationships into fantasy and delusion, and a sense of mental fragmentation.
Claustrophobia: extreme or irrational fear of confined places.
Kleptomania: a recurrent urge to steal, typically without regard for need or profit.
Megalomania: obsession with the exercise of power.

One word substitutions.question: ২৪) A place where bees are kept in called-
One word substitutions.exp:
An apiary: a place where bees are kept.
A mole: a small burrowing mammal with dark velvety fur, a long muzzle, and very small eyes, feeding mainly on worms, grubs, and other invertebrates.
A hive: a thing that has the domed shape of a beehive.
A sanctuary: refuge or safety from pursuit, persecution, or other danger.

One word substitutions.question: ২৫) A place that provides refuge-
One word substitutions.exp:
Asylum: the protection granted by a state to someone who has left their home country as a political refugee.
Sanatorium: an establishment for the medical treatment of people who are convalescing or have a chronic illness.
Shelter: a place giving temporary protection from bad weather or danger.
Orphanage: a residential institution for the care and education of orphans.

One word substitutions.question: ২৬) Paper written by hand-
One word substitutions.exp:
Handicraft: activity involving the making of decorative domestic or other objects by hand.
Manuscript: a book, document, or piece of music written by hand rather than typed or printed.
Handiwork: making things by hand, considered as a subject of instruction.
Thesis: a statement or theory that is put forward as a premise to be maintained or proved.

One word substitutions.question: ২৭) One who is fond of fighting-
One word substitutions.exp:
Bellicose: demonstrating aggression and willingness to fight.
Aggressive: ready or likely to attack or confront
Belligerent: engaged in a war or conflict, as recognized by international law.
Militant: favouring confrontational or violent methods in support of a political or social cause.

One word substitutions.question: ২৮) State in which the few govern the many-
One word substitutions.exp:
Monarchy: a form of government with a monarch at the head.
Oligarchy: a small group of people having control of a country or organization.
Plutocracy: a state or society governed by the wealthy.
Autocracy: a system of government by one person with absolute power.

One word substitutions.question: ২৯) Habitually silent or talking little-
One word substitutions.exp:
Taciturn - tending to be silent and uncommunicative, reticent.
Synopsis - a summary of a piece of writing, a play etc.
Unequivocal - expressing your opinion or intention very clearly and firmly (unambiguous).
Servile - wanting too much to please somebody and obey them (fawning).

One word substitutions.question: ৩০) A person of good understanding knowledge and reasoning power-
One word substitutions.exp:
Expert: a person who is very knowledgeable about or skilful in a particular area.
Intellectual: Intelligent; knowledgeable.
Snob: a person with an exaggerated respect for high social position or wealth who seeks to associate with social superiors and looks down on those regarded as socially inferior.
Literate: able to read and write.

One word substitutions.question: ৩১) One who collects coins as hobby-
One word substitutions.exp:
Philatelist: a person who collects or studies stamps.
Ornithologist: a person who studies or is an expert on birds.
Statistician: an expert in the preparation and analysis of statistics.
Numismatist: someone who studies or collects coins, paper money, or medals.

One word substitutions.question: ৩২) That which cannot be seen-
One word substitutions.exp:
Intangible - that exists, but that is difficult to describe, understand or measure.
Insensible - unable to feel something or react to it.
Invisible - means which things we can't see and we can't hear.

One word substitutions.question: ৩৩) Lasting only for a very short time:-
One word substitutions.exp:
Transparent : easy to perceive or detect.
Temporal : relating to worldly as opposed to spiritual affairs; secular.
Temperate : showing moderation or self-restraint.
Temporary : Lasting only for a very short time.

One word substitutions.question: ৩৪) A person living permanently in a certain place-
One word substitutions.exp:
A person living permanently in a certain place- Domicile.
এখানে, ব্যক্তিকে নির্দেশ করা হয়নি, বরং একজন ব্যক্তির নির্দিষ্ট স্থায়ী বাসস্থান কে নির্দেশ করা হয়েছে,
তাই এর এক কোথায় প্রকাশ হবে Domicile (a person's residence or home).
Resident- বাসিন্দা (ব্যক্তি)।
Native - স্থানীয় (ব্যক্তি)।
Domicile - স্থায়ী বাসস্থান।

One word substitutions.question: ৩৫) Bringing about gentle and painless death from incurable disease-
One word substitutions.exp:
Suicide: the action of killing oneself intentionally.
Euphoria: a feeling or state of intense excitement and happiness.
Gallows: a structure, typically of two uprights and a crosspiece, for the hanging of criminals.
Euthanasia: the painless killing of a patient suffering from an incurable and painful disease or in an irreversible coma.

One word substitutions.question: ৩৬) An office for which no salary is paid-
One word substitutions.exp:
Hospitable : অতিথিসেবাপরায়ণ,অতিথিবত্সল
Honorary : অবৈতনিক
Gratis : বিনামূল্যে

One word substitutions.question: ৩৭) One who able to use the right and left hands equally well-
One word substitutions.exp:
Sinister : One who is able to use the left hand well.
Ambivalent : having mixed feelings or contradictory ideas about something or someone.
Amateur : a person who is contemptibly inept at a particular activity.
Ambidextrous : able to use the right and left hands equally well.

One word substitutions.question: ৩৮) One who is not easily pleased by anything-
One word substitutions.exp:
Maiden: an Unmarried girl or woman.
Mediaeval: related to middle ages.

One word substitutions.question: ৩৯) A disease that spreads over a large area-
One word substitutions.exp:
Academic : relating to education and scholarship.
Incorrigible : not able to be changed or reformed.
Invincible : too powerful to be defeated or overcome.
Epidemic : a widespread occurrence of an infectious disease in a community at a particular time.

One word substitutions.question: ৪০) A person interested in collecting, studying and selling of old things
One word substitutions.exp:
Antiquarian - dealing in rare books.
Archaeologist - study of ancient cultures.

One word substitutions.question: ৪১) A person who pretends to have more knowledge or skill than he really has-
One word substitutions.exp:
Crook : a person who is dishonest or a criminal.
Apotheosis : the elevation of someone to divine status.
Renegade : a person who deserts and betrays an organization, country, or set of principles.
Charlatan : a person falsely claiming to have a special knowledge or skill.

One word substitutions.question: ৪২) One who eats everything-
One word substitutions.exp:
Omnivorous:one who eats both plants and animals.
Omniscient means the one who knows or seems to know everything.

One word substitutions.question: ৪৩) International destruction of racial groups-
One word substitutions.exp:
Matricide : the killing of one's mother.
Regicide : the action of killing a king.
Homicide : the killing of one person by another.
Genocide : the deliberate killing of a large group of people, especially those of a particular nation or ethnic group.

One word substitutions.question: ৪৪) One who possesses many talents
One word substitutions.exp: Versatile means multitalented, multiskilled no matter if the talents are exceptional or not whereas gifted means having exceptional talent.

One word substitutions.question: ৪৫) A person who is indifferent to pains and pleasures of life.
One word substitutions.exp:
Sadist : the tendency to derive pleasure, especially sexual gratification, from inflicting pain, suffering, or humiliation on others.
Psychiatrist : a medical practitioner specializing in the diagnosis and treatment of mental illness.
Aristocrat : a member of the aristocracy.
Stoic : a person who can endure pain or hardship without showing their feelings or complaining.

One word substitutions.question: ৪৬) A prima facie case is such-
One word substitutions.option1: ক) As it seems at first sight
One word substitutions.option2: খ) As it is made to seem at first sight
One word substitutions.option3: গ) As it turns out to be at the end
One word substitutions.option4: ঘ) As it seems to the court after a number of hearings
One word substitutions.exp: In common practice the term prima facie is used to describe the apparent nature of something upon initial observation.

One word substitutions.question: ৪৭) One who believes in the power of fate:
One word substitutions.exp:
Optimist: hopefulness and confidence about the future or the success of something.
Pessimist: a tendency to see the worst aspect of things or believe that the worst will happen.
Parsimonious: very unwilling to spend money or use resources.
Fatalist: the belief that all events are predetermined and therefore inevitable.

One word substitutions.question: ৪৮) Land so surrounded by water as to be almost an island-
One word substitutions.exp:
Archipelago: an extensive group of islands.
Isthmus: a narrow strip of land with sea on either side, forming a link between two larger areas of land.
Peninsula: a piece of land almost surrounded by water or projecting out into a body of water.
Lagoon: a stretch of salt water separated from the sea by a low sandbank or coral reef.

One word substitutions.question: ৪৯) A hater of knowledge and learning-
One word substitutions.exp:
Bibliophile: a person who collects or has a great love for books.
Philologist: learner of language, or linguist.
Misogynist: a person who hates women.
Misologist: a hater of knowledge and learning.

One word substitutions.question: ৫০) The study of ancient societies-
One word substitutions.exp:
Anthropology: The study of humans in the past and present.
Archeology: The study of ancient societies, done by looking at tools, bones, buildings, and other things from that time that have been found.
History: The study of the past, particularly how it relates to humans.
Ethnology: The branch of anthropology that compares and analyzes the characteristics of different peoples and the relationship between them.
